Suspicious hands: player 1001

Opponents he beats more than expected

Each opponent he played heads-up gets a pair score. The score compares his results against that opponent with:

  • his results against everyone else
  • everyone else's results against that opponent

How to read the score:

  • Around 0: normal.
  • 3 or more, and in the top 1% of all pairs: the opponent is listed here. He may be seeing this opponent's cards.
  • A listed opponent is a reason to review their hands together, not a finding.
  • Pair ranks are within the reference sample.

First table: how he plays against this opponent

  • Hands, bb/100, Showdowns won: his results against this opponent.
  • z columns: how unusual each part is (win rate, showdowns, calls, bets, all-ins, preflop, folds). Around 0 is normal; 2 or more stands out.
  • Score: all parts combined.
  • Pair: where this pair ranks among all pairs in the reference sample.

How to read this page
  • Each flagged hand is shown in full: the actions on every street, the board, both players' cards and the result.
  • Hands are flagged by the four rules in the key, using the player's equity against the opponent's real hand.
  • Flagged hands are ranked by the Equity review, largest contradiction first.
  • A flag is a reason to review a hand, not a finding.
Why some flagged folds look normal
  • Rules A and D flag a fold whenever the opponent held the better hand. They ignore the bet size and the pot odds.
  • An honest player often folds in the same spot.
  • These hands rank low. In 24 of the 52 A and D folds, the predicted range also says fold.
Real cards beyond the range
  • His turn and river folds follow the opponent's real cards more closely than those of 93% of comparable players in the reference sample.

Player 1001: 718 hands analysed, 74 flagged (10.3%).

About the comparisons on this page
  • Player 1001 is compared with a reference sample: a sample of players from a larger full-information population.
  • Percentiles, pair ranks and the predicted range all come from that sample.
  • Treat them as a limited snapshot. They are more reliable on full population data.

Last 15 days: 27 suspicious of 250 hands (10.8%): ESCALATE for manual review.

Key

Flag rules (equity against the opponent's real hand):

  • A. River fold when beaten: folds on the river facing a bet with 0% equity.
  • B. River bluff-catch: calls or raises on the river facing a bet with 99.9% equity or more.
  • C. Successful river bluff: bets the river with under 50% equity and every opponent folds.
  • D. Early fold near dead: folds on the flop or turn with under 10% equity.

Equity review (box under each hand):

  • Shows the player's equity against all hands, against the opponent's predicted range and against the real hand, with the pot odds.
  • The predicted range is the opponent's likely hands based on his betting. It is also shown as a 13 × 13 grid and as text.
  • Equity values are samples. The predicted range was fitted on the reference sample, so treat it as a limited snapshot.

Other:

  • Decision times are shown for context. They were not used to flag or rank hands.
  • Rows for player 1001 are in red. Times are UTC.
Postflop
  • First, the 74 hands flagged by rules A–D, ranked by the Equity review.
  • Then, 3 rare flop decisions: decisions that matched the opponent's real hand and that other players rarely make with the same strength against the same betting.
    • Folds facing a bet with under 20% equity, where other players fold less than half the time.
    • Calls of a bet while ahead, where other players call less than 30% of the time.
  • Flop decisions already shown above are not repeated.
